title: model-loading-failed-breadcrumbs-aisha-rahman
body:
Quick breadcrumb-style notes for the model loading failure on dedicated pool (nv4).

Context: trying to load open-model-XL-3b (safetensors sharded checkpoint) in production-like env: pt 2.2, safetensors 0.3.2, bitsandbytes 0.41, accelerate 0.21.0. Loading path is gs://redwood-models/open-model-xl-3b/safetensors/ (8 shards + index).

Observed failure (first seen 2024-11-02): runtime fails during final merge of shards with a cryptic safetensors error and then OOM on worker. Logs below.

Commands tried (local repro, then on dedicated node):
- gsutil -m cp -r gs://redwood-models/open-model-xl-3b/safetensors ./open-model-xl-3b/
- python -c "from safetensors import safe_open; f=safe_open('open-model-xl-3b/model.safetensors', framework='pt'); print(list(f.keys())[:10])"  # FAIL on node: SafetensorError
- python -c "import torch; d=torch.load('open-model-xl-3b/pytorch_model-00001-of-00008.bin', map_location='cpu'); print(next(iter(d.items()))[0])"  # sometimes raises EOFError
- hf_hub download: hf_hub.download(repo_id, filename=...) -> some shards downloaded truncated (size mismatch)

Error snippets (copied from dedicated node logs):
- safetensors.errors.SafetensorError: bad header: expected 0x7374 but got 0x0000
- RuntimeError: EOFError: Ran out of bytes while reading tensor data (expected 24903680, got 0)
- ValueError: Unexpected end of file while deserializing tensor metadata
- PyTorchBackend: load_state_dict returned missing keys: ['transformer.h.23.attn.k_proj.weight']  # inconsistent shapes reported

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Corrupted shard(s) on GCS (partial upload or network interruption). Some shards have correct size, others are 0 bytes or truncated.
2) Index file (model.safetensors.index.json) mismatches the shard set (e.g., older index pointing to different file names / counts).
3) Transfer tool (gsutil / hf_hub) is silently truncating when retries > 0 or when preempted; checksum not enforced on our side.
4) Worker file system (tmpfs) OOMs mid-copy causing truncated files and subsequent safetensors failure. Node showed ephemeral disk at 95% during download.
5) Version incompatibility: safetensors header changes between versions; but same code loads in local dev (my laptop) with safetensors 0.2.x — unlikely but keep in mind.

What I checked so far: 
- ls -l on GCS copy vs local copy: some shards show identical size, but model-00005-of-00008.safetensors on node was 0 bytes.
- md5sum of shards (on the source bucket) vs downloads: md5 mismatch for 00005. Source md5: 3b1f8c..., downloaded md5: 000000... (empty).
- Re-downloaded the shard multiple times -> sometimes succeeds, sometimes fails. Pattern: failures correlate with high node disk usage and simultaneous downloads (~8 shards at once).
- Tried serial download (one shard at a time) -> success so far. Parallel (gsutil -m cp) reproduces failure quickly.
- Tried using `gcloud storage cp` -> same truncated shard occasionally.
- Using `curl -O` from public presigned url (signed for 30m) -> seems stable.

Temporary mitigations applied: 
- Switched downloader in the orchestration job to serial copy per shard (throttle downloads to 2 concurrent). Reduced failures (but increases startup time).
- Added a pre-check step to validate shard sizes against index file before loading. If mismatch -> abort and retry download.
- Added disk usage check on node (fail early if free < 10GB).

Notes on metadata/index mismatch:
- index file content (excerpt): {"weight_map": {"transformer.h.0.attn.q_proj.weight":"pytorch_model-00001-of-00008.safetensors:0"}}  # need to ensure our loader supports this mapping format
- Some checkpoints in the bucket have both .safetensors and .bin shards; the index file produced by export script sometimes lists bin shards while directory contains safetensors. Potentially a packaging bug in export pipeline.

Repro steps for infra/QA:
1) On a fresh dedicated instance with same AMI, try parallel gsutil -m cp of the 8 shards -> observe truncated shard(s) ~50% of runs.
2) Re-run with serial cp -> success.
3) Attempt to copy using signed HTTPS (curl) concurrently -> success. Suggests gsutil/multi-threading + node disk interplay.

Potential fixes (engineering):
- Make downloader pipeline use ranged HTTP GETs (curl) with checksum verification, or use hf_hub with explicit checksum check. Avoid aggressive parallel downloads to local ephemeral.
- Add per-shard sha256 stored in the model metadata (s3/gcs object metadata) and verify after download. 
- Improve exporter to generate a canonical index file that matches files in bucket (fail export if mismatch).
- Add safetensors header/version guard in loader and a clearer error message pointing to shard corruption vs version mismatch.

Observations / oddities: 
- On node with kernel 5.15, doing 8 concurrent downloads saturated IOPS and kernel returned EINTR to gsutil process occasionally (not obvious in logs).
- When a shard is truncated, safetensors often reports header mismatch (0x0000) — consistent with zero-byte files.
- Some customers previously reported similar failure when using preemptible instances during model pull (maybe same underlying cause).

Open TODOs / next actions: 
- [ ] Add per-shard checksum verification in downloader (high priority).
- [ ] Update export pipeline to include size+sha256 in model metadata and include in index file.
- [ ] Add robust retry/backoff for partial downloads that validates size before proceeding to load.
- [ ] Run a 48-hour stress with concurrent model pulls to reproduce and gather kernel-level metrics (disk queue, IOPS).
- [ ] Write a short postmortem draft if we hit customer impact (track JIRA-MLINF-310).

Notes to self: slack thread with Jordan/Maya had a note about bad GCS object created during last export (Oct 30). Need to check export job logs: export-2024-10-30-23:42 (pipeline: model-export-service).

Previous related bugs: 
- GH-4572: safetensors load crashes with truncated file (resolved by adding file size check).
- GH-4698: export pipeline sometimes omitted index update (race during atomic rename). Might be related.

If I get more logs will paste here. For now, serial downloads + size checks is the practical stopgap.

Commands & snippets I want to keep handy:
- verify sizes: python -c "import json,os; idx=json.load(open('model.safetensors.index.json')); sizes=[os.path.getsize(p.split(':')[0]) for p in idx['weight_map'].values()]; print(sizes)"
- compute local sha256: sha256sum pytorch_model-00005-of-00008.safetensors
- quick safetensors inspect: python -c "from safetensors import safe_open; print(safe_open('pytorch_model-00001-of-00008.safetensors','pt').keys())"
